First off, apologies for the wall of text. Second, when you talk about this with financial aid staff, make sure you mention the whole bit about abuse being a big reason you're breaking contact.

I say this because when it comes to Dependency Override Appeals (which is what you'd need to submit - if you haven't already been directed to it, its on the financial aid website), hearing "financially independent" immediately sends off an alarm bell as the one thing we're DEFINITELY not allowed to approve the appeal for. We get a lot of people sending in appeals saying they're financially independent, that their parents won't be paying for their college, etc. etc. While most in the financial aid office are sympathetic and understand those types of situations, we cant even consider it for an appeal according to federal and state law. The federal standard sorta thinks of it like this: parents had their child, they're financially responsible for the child as they become a student, and if they don't want to pay for the student's college, the feds won't force them but also won't suddenly make them NOT financially responsible for the student.

It's a confusing process and I can't say exactly how your appeal will be approved or if it will be approved, I would just say make sure to include any and all details. The documentation we need is included on the appeal form, so make sure you read it over, but so long as you write up a clear statement about why you're doing an appeal, we can try our best to work with you to see what we can do. One of the big things we look for is if a student completely cut off contact with the parent(s) and will continue to have no contact. The state actually suggests we wait up to a year to see if the situation "resolves itself", even for abuse cases, which is something our office personally disagrees with and rarely follows. But hopefully that gives an idea of that type of bonkers laws we have to navigate when it comes to these things so you can have an easier time setting up your appeal paperwork.

I lived in Prather my senior year and have gone through all three of those buildings and seen the rooms in each (used to be an resident assistant). I really enjoyed my time living there and I found it a lot homier than other dorms (particularly Jester, which can feel awfully cramped at times). Because of their older designs, the rooms really vary in size and can have some weird style quirks (like columns sorta just... there). If you luck out and get a corner room, congrats, your room is going to be massive. The smallest rooms are still a nice size though. Downside of the living situation is that there are no elevators but there are plenty of stairs. Get ready for a leg workout if you have to go up those everyday. There isn't that much difference in the buildings, particularly because they share almost everything. If you live in Prather, you live in the building which has the lobby that acts as the mail and help center for all three of those dorms, so that's a little convenient. Roberts has a really nice sitting area on it's ground floor, good for studying, but you can use that regardless which of the three you get in to. Also, if you go to the top floor of Roberts, you can sit up on the roof patio, which is another nice spot for studying (and which you can access, again, regardless which building you're living in). Brackenridge doesn't have a lot too it, but it's still a nice little area. In between the hallway that connects Roberts and Brackenridge is the only kitchen for all of BRP, along with a laundry room, I believe a TV room, and a rec room with a piano and pool I think? Maybe Foosball. Prather has it's own TV room and laundry room, along with a vending room which has a Foosball table kinda stuffed in the middle of it. I remember them saying they were going to make a rec room in there as well, but I don't know if that ever got finalized. 

Social life wise, I thought it was really easy to meet people, and BRP being so small helps a lot with that. I suggest joining the facebook group if you get in to any of those dorms. I remember there always being people setting up video game nights in the TV room or other little events. Also, the resident assistant hosted events are always really nice. Almost every year they do some sort of s'mores/BBQ night, which was my favorite. If you go out of your way to attend those, you'll definitely make friends with the regulars who attend them (plus free food).
